topic: Floating-Point Arithmetic Operations and Instruction Set Architecture
explanation: Floating-point arithmetic is crucial for scientific computing and many other applications.  Understanding how the processor handles these operations at the instruction level is essential for writing efficient and correct systems-level code.  The instruction set architecture (ISA) defines the specific instructions available for floating-point operations, influencing performance and code structure.  Different ISAs (e.g., x86-64 with AVX2) provide varying levels of support and performance for floating-point computations.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; x86-64 AVX (8x Single-Precision Add)
; YMM registers (256-bit)
vmovups (%rdi), %ymm0  ; Load 8 A floats
vmovups (%rsi), %ymm1  ; Load 8 B floats
vaddps %ymm1, %ymm0, %ymm2 ; YMM0 + YMM1 -> YMM2
vmovups %ymm2, (%rdx)  ; Store result

; Fused Multiply-Add (FMA) for Precision/Latency
; Compute (A*B + C) in one step
; Using vfmadd213sd (Dest=XMM0)
vmovsd (%rdi), %xmm0   ; C (Operand 3)
vmovsd (%rsi), %xmm1   ; B (Operand 2)
vmovsd (%rdx), %xmm2   ; A (Operand 1)
; C = A*B + C
vfmadd213sd %xmm0, %xmm1, %xmm2
keywords: FPU, Floating Point ISA, FP instruction set, SIMD floating point
